subjects.displayTitle: The mystery of sacrifice: a life that gives life
subjects.introduction: Sacrifice sounds like loss until one asks what it makes possible. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that what must be given up is the tangle of blameworthy qualities, not life itself, which is to be kept alive in praise and service. What fills the emptied place is mercy, kindness, forgiveness and the power to give life to other spirits. His images carry the paradox: iron in fire takes on the fire’s qualities, a candle spends itself in light, and a seed, like the grain of wheat in John’s Gospel [1], loses its form so that a whole tree can appear. Paul’s living offering [2] shows how a life with its particular abilities becomes such a gift, and the Qur’anic account of Abraham and his son [3] keeps trial and ransom in view. The practice is as ordinary as nursing a sick friend or yielding a cherished opinion for unity’s sake, and as costly as lives remembered under persecution. From here the way runs through detachment, through tests and trials, and on to the sacrifice of the Manifestation of God that gives the world life.

I beseech Thee with the beseeching of one abased before the Kingdom of the Glorious One, and I implore Thee with the imploring of one evanescent before the All-Merciful Horizon, with my tongue and my heart crying continuously unto the Concourse on High, and I say:

O Lord, O Lord! Calamity hath encompassed all regions, and the earth hath quaked from successive afflictions visited upon humanity. The forces of dust and the pillars of verdure have trembled as the fires of tyranny and aggression have blazed forth, reaching unto the heavens.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: Verily they have dealt with the people of oppression with the utmost amity and forgiveness and they rejoice over their trials.
O God! these, their enemies did not know; if they knew they would [not] have acted in this manner. This has ever been their custom in the past ages.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: O Lord! Bestow upon me a drop from that brimming cup, and waft to my nostrils a fragrance from that garden of sacrifice, that I may be attracted to all horizons, become bewildered and enchanted by that resplendent Beauty, and offer up my soul and spirit.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: She traveled in Your path to distant regions and proclaimed Your Kingdom in various lands until her flesh and fat melted away from the hardships she endured in Your path. She was afflicted with illnesses and diseases that weakened her body, made her bones brittle and inflamed her insides, until the pains intensified in her heart, whereupon she left this transient life, yearning for the eternal life.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: O Lord! She believed in You and Your verses, was attracted by Your fragrances, recited Your verses and words, gave glad tidings of the dawning of the Sun of Your divine Oneness, called out Your name in Your kingdom, left her homeland, distanced herself from family and friends, bore every hardship and suffering, and found sweet the bitterness of separation - all out of love for teaching children and passion for educating girls in the farthest lands.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: And he departed out of his fatherland with his two sons, setting his face towards Thee, trusting wholly in Thee, attracted to the Divine Fragrance of Thy days, and yielding thanks for Thy bounties. He traversed the valleys and the plains and crossed the rugged grounds and the mountains enduring every toil and affliction until, while on his way, he surrendered his soul and drank deep of the chalice of sacrifice that brimmeth over with the pleasing choice Wine and he yielded up his breath to Thee while being inflamed with the fire of his longing for Thee and attracted to the Day-Star of Thy creation.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: He sacrificed his life repeatedly in Thy path and yearned for death in his longing to meet Thee, until he fulfilled his covenant while beseeching and supplicating before Thee, longing to attain Thy presence and yearning to ascend to Thy sacred threshold.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: Finally, he was exiled to Hadba', where he could no longer bear the separation from his Lord, so he set off on foot, in the utmost poverty, and eagerly while chanting prayers he walked from Hadba' to 'Akka. His [body] could, however, not bear the hardships of the journey; he travelled across the deserts with no food or provisions, and surrendered his soul with the utmost fervour and longing.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: Thou art he who didst leave thy homeland out of love for God, the Lord of the seen and the unseen, and didst depart from thy house in longing for His presence, until at last thou didst surrender thy spirit in His love and good-pleasure.

order.why: Allow lament and bereavement their full voice, then move through remembrance, prayer, protection and hope for those who remain.
shortened: We testify that he hath taken for himself, beneath the canopies of My grandeur, a station whereunto none hath attained save him who hath sacrificed his spirit and all that he possessed in the path of God, the Lord of all religions.

shortened: He passed his days in bitterness and bore the blame of every unbearable ill-omened one. This was solely out of love for Thy beauty, seeking reunion with Thee, yearning for the proximity of Thy mercy, pursuing Thy face, and longing to meet Thee.

shortened: The purpose is this: it was the wish of that departed one to sacrifice himself. Praise be to God that he attained unto this gift, was exhilarated with this cup of favours and hastened unto the invisible kingdom of oneness in the utmost joy and gladness.

shortened: His honor Fa'iz has ascended to the Supreme Horizon. His honor the Ismu'llahu'l-Asdaq, upon him be the Most Glorious Glory of God, was always intimate with this exalted Cause and coupled with sacrifice. He never rested nor laid his head upon the pillow of comfort.

shortened: Thou seest Thy loved ones, detached from their homes, turning toward the seat of Thy mighty throne, fleeing from Thy enemies to the shelter of Thy mercy and favors. They have borne hardships by land and sea, drawing nigh unto Thee and seeking the sweet-scented breezes of Thy nearness and presence.

shortened: I continually offer praise and supplication at the threshold of the All-Knowing Lord and beseech boundless aid and grace for those blessed souls, that they may raise a fresh tumult and become the cause of increased spirit and fragrance for the martyred spirits in the Most Glorious Kingdom, so that those noble fathers may witness how their righteous sons are watering the field of their hopes - that is, the crop which those fathers planted, these sons are watering; the palm tree which they planted, these are nurturing.

shortened: Well then, these servants must now follow the example of those essences of being, showing such self-sacrifice in the path of the Intended Lord that it becomes evident and manifest that these souls are indeed the worthy successors of those noble predecessors and are the manifestation of "the son is the mystery of his father" in the gathering of the horizons.

shortened: That which is most precious is most worthy of being sacrificed. A precious possession, not a worthless thing, is fit to be offered up. The most precious of all things is a piece of one's liver, especially a son in the sight of his father and mother. Give thanks unto God that thou didst sacrifice the most precious of things in the path of God and didst offer up the light of thine eyes.

shortened: A mother who sacrifices such a precious gem in the path of God is herself a pearl from the shell of faith and certitude and a brilliant jewel from the ocean of grace and bounty.

shortened: Thus all that is related to the loved ones of God--their former glory, their present services, the grievous sufferings they have borne--all will, even as carving on slabs of emerald, be recorded on the scrolls of the Abha Kingdom, and therefrom will they shed their radiance upon all the worlds of God.

He was persecuted, O my God, by all peoples and enemies, and was burned by the fire of their hatred blazing to the heavens.

shortened: Make me the target for arrows aimed at Thy loved ones and the mark for spears directed at the hearts of Thy chosen ones, that I may sacrifice for them my spirit, essence, body, being, reality and identity.

shortened: For through calamity the heart of Abdul-Baha is attracted; through (suffering) oppression the breast of Abdul-Baha is dilated; through enduring afflictions the faithfulness of Abdul-Baha is proven; through imprisonment the soul of Abdul-Baha is cheered; at every moment he wishes to quaff the cup of sacrifice in the path of God.

shortened: Notwithstanding the weakness of constitution, the infirmity of the body and the nervous fever, every night He was in a city and each day amongst a community. Although at times He could not speak one word, before large audiences He delivered lengthy addresses.

shortened: Service to the Blessed Threshold requireth one to sacrifice everything. In that state, I gave her up and entrusted her to the Blessed Beauty, proceeding with the sea voyage, for I am completely resigned [to His Will].

shortened: My health, comfort, life and death are of no importance - may a hundred thousand like me be sacrificed for a single hair of the Temple of God's Cause.

shortened: For the past few years I have had no rest by day or night. I have been working constantly. Often in the middle of night when I was in bed, they would bring to me the word that such and such a person had called and I would get up and dress again to receive him.

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: Rather, imprisonment in the path of the Beloved is a palace, and chains and bonds are freedom in both worlds, and fetters and manacles are the crown of endless sovereignty and grandeur.

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: In any case, we exiles are in utmost contentment and joy, even yearning and longing for sacrifice. O Lord! Ordain for Thy poor and helpless servant to drink from that cup which overflows with Thy great bounty....

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: Those holy souls whose servitude 'Abdu'l-Baha seeks as eternal glory - they all endured the utmost trials and tribulations. Is it befitting and proper loyalty that I should seek comfort and ease, or freedom from prison? No, by God, this is not faithfulness in God's Cause!...

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: This physical and spiritual existence of 'Abdu'l-Baha was brought into being only to be effaced and annihilated in the path of Baha'u'llah. Otherwise what fruit is there from existence? Surely non-existence would be better than such an existence. This is true love, this is annihilation in the path of God....

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: Sacrifice! How sweet is the word in my taste! There is no greater bounty than this for me!

What greater glory can I conceive than to see this neck chained for His sake, these feet fettered for His love, this body mutilated or thrown into the depths of the sea for His Cause! If in reality we are His sincere lovers - if in reality I am His sincere Servant, then I must sacrifice my life, my all at His Blessed Threshold.

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: What is life but to be immolated on the Altar of His Love! What is life but to be thrown in the dust of the feet of the beloved ones, what is this worthless will but to be surrendered into the hands of the Almighty Father. What is the soul but to be offered in the arena of Truth, what is the spirit but to be given up for the progress of divine Civilization and universal Peace, and what is rest and comfort but to be thrown away for the establishment of brotherhood and the spiritualization of mankind!

order.why: Hear personal devotion and the burdens of service in their original letters and reports, including the questions, family circumstances and prison settings.
shortened: Because calamities encountered in God's pathway are, to Abdu'l-Baha, but favour and grace, and in one of His Tablets the all-glorious Beauty hath declared: 'I never passed a tree but Mine heart addressed it saying: "O would that thou wert cut down in My name, and My body crucified upon thee!"' These were the words of the Most Great Name.

O ye that thirst after Him! Strip yourselves of every earthly affection, and hasten to embrace your Beloved.

shortened:
If thou fulfillest, it shall be fulfilled:
To drink the cup of woe from every chalice,
To taste the blood of grief from every heart,
To sever hope from touch of any comfort,
To cut desire from reach of any need,
To shed one's blood in passion's path is duty,
To burn the heart in love was my first pact,
Sleepless nights from every stinging bite,
Daily abuse is part of my tradition,
Deadly poison is my drink divine,
Fate's oppression is my mercy true.
Abandon love's claim or accept what comes -
Thus runs the law within my holy way."

This is the way of the path - if you seek union with Baha
If you're not fit for this path, stay far and bring no trouble

If it is in accord with Thy divine wisdom, bestow upon me good health and encircle me with Thine own Confirmation and assistance; - in order that I may sacrifice my life on Thy Path, concentrate all my energies in Thy service, unfurl the banner of international Peace over every region, unclose the signs of Thy Mercy and Bestowal to the people of the world and summon mankind to the banquet of Thy inexhaustible Bounties.

questions: What changes in your understanding of sacrifice when the opening passages connect it with transformed character, care for life and patient service? Which later passage most deepens or challenges that understanding?

What do the images of iron and fire, seed and tree, candle and light help you see about the relation between selfhood and spiritual growth? Where do their different emphases lead you toward new questions?

How do the examples of nursing, hospitality, family responsibility, small gifts and relinquishing an opinion make sacrifice concrete? How might the reciprocal responsibility of those who receive help shape a community’s practice?

How does a passage’s setting—as prayer, personal counsel, poetry, recollection or an account of persecution—affect the way you read its language? What do the fuller contexts reveal about grief, courage and the purposes for which a life is offered?

What connections and differences emerge when you read John 12:23–26, Romans 12:1–8 and Qur’an 37:100–111 beside this compilation? How do fruitfulness, living service, trial and ransom open different paths into the mystery?

What might it mean to assess sacrifice through the life and well-being it helps make possible? Which connected subject—detachment, courage, tests and trials, martyrdom, prayer for sacrifice, or the redemptive sacrifice of the Manifestation—would help you pursue your next question?

references.label: 1 · John 12:23–26 · The seed and its fruit
references.note: Read these verses in the King James Version, keeping the image of the grain of wheat with Jesus’ words about life, service and following Him. Compare them with the explanations here in which the seed’s qualities appear in a tree and the perfections of Christ become manifest in a community. What does the image reveal about continuity within change? How does attending to the fruit alter the meaning of what is given up? Explore both the Gospel’s particular setting and the ways these Bahá’í passages interpret the relation between Christ’s life, His sacrifice and the lives of those who follow Him.

references.label: 2 · Romans 12:1–8 · A living offering
references.note: Paul moves from the offering of a living body and the renewal of the mind to humility, a body with many members, and different gifts expressed in service. Read the King James Version through verse 8, including teaching, giving and mercy. Place it beside this collection’s descriptions of sacrifice as transformed qualities and useful work. How might a whole life become an offering through the particular abilities of each person? What place do discernment, humility and mutual dependence have in such a life? Consider the connections while keeping Paul’s account of life in Christ and the Bahá’í explanations in their own terms.
references.verified: Read Romans 12:1–8 in full, King James Version, Bible Gateway, 2026-10-10. Verified living sacrifice, renewed mind, sober judgment, one body and distinct gifts.

references.label: 3 · Qur’an 37:100–111 · Trust, trial and ransom
references.note: Follow the verse links from 100 through 111, using the Sahih International translation alongside the other translations provided. The sequence moves from a prayer for a righteous child to the father’s dream, the son’s response, their submission, the declaration that the vision is fulfilled, and ransom. The son is not named within these verses. Compare this sequence with the collection’s references to Abraham, Isaac, Ishmael and the continuing mystery of sacrifice. How do willingness, trial, divine response and remembrance shape the story? What becomes clearer when a later allusion is read with the whole scriptural episode, including its ending?
